system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of source material:** Seller's draft and Disclosure Letter are counterparty documents. Nothing in them is treated as "agreed", "settled" or "adequate" merely because the Seller says so (playbook 0.4 / 6.3). Notably, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update: it confirms several things the Update glosses over (no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark payout, bonuses omitted from funds flow, no title verification by Buyer). We should rely on those admissions.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure coincides with our conditional fallback, but no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft exists, so the fallback is not available – a matching number is not clearance.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once basket exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the excess-only structure converts the basket into a deductible, materially eroding recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months; plus a drafting rider that any limitation applies to *all* Claims unless expressly excluded.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; hold at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" rider.** 18 months is only a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the rider is a back-door general-regime override (see N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright.** Collapsing title/capacity into a 20%/18-month regime would leave the Buyer unable to recover the price if it does not actually get the shares – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No fraud carve-out appears; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert express carve-out as a non-negotiable.** The Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording purports to limit fraud, which no one on our side has authority to accept.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sched 7 / DL [1.1]–[1.2] – whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records generally disclosed.
- **Buyer wants:** Only specific, fair disclosure (matter identified with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to assess its nature and effect); no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT [1.1] and [1.2]; accept only the specific disclosures in sections 2–10 and only insofar as they are fair.** General disclosure of 11 data-room folders and public records would qualify every warranty by material we have not been required to find.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything *discoverable* from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any residual qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named seller-side knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT and delete.** "Discoverable" and "advisers" extends the bar to constructive knowledge and would effectively swallow the warranty package.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – "addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. **DL §2 admits no final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.**
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring an *effective* consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 **and** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not satisfied on mere delivery; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft as a hard CP with evidence of conditions satisfied.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms the consent does not yet exist.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". **DL §3 admits not repaid, no final discharge.**
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark; repayment direct from Completion funds; effective security releases (cl 9.2 discharge) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; require payout + direct repayment + releases at Completion.** A debt-free/cash-free deal cannot close with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company and the discharge in the Seller's gift.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics"; DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised. **DL §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.**
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item deducted from the price or paid by Seller at Completion; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insist on a specific seller-funded line item incl. on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism – once Completion occurs the Company carries the liability unless the funds flow deals with it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broader indemnity covering loss from any failure of SOW3 (and related) IP to vest in the Company, third-party claims and cure costs, while preserving the cl 7.3 cure (pay and obtain assignment). Seek bank evidence of payment status and a confirmatory assignment at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; broaden indemnity and require pre-Completion cure or escrow.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way, so the indemnity must cover the title-to-IP risk, not just a payment amount.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sched 6 – "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL §6: link sent to unintended external address, ~1,240 records, access/scope/notification undetermined.
- **Buyer wants:** Preservation of logs, completed investigation with regular written updates, a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (uncapped by general basket), and a pre-Completion update warranty. Do **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric exposure in either direction.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "not material" characterisation as unsupported; require investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure confirms the facts are not yet established, so materiality cannot be asserted either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals, AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000), "ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8: read DD-008 and DD-011 together; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of each renewal (timing, termination rights, accrual, whether committed pre- or post-Locked Box/Completion). No automatic Debt classification or price deduction unless the assessment supports it.
- **Recommendation: HOLD – do not accept "ordinary course"; request the DD-008/DD-011 documents and renewal terms before agreeing treatment.** The Seller's characterisation is unsupported by its own disclosure, but our playbook does not pre-judge the outcome either.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 rider ("any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") plus cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") and "Tax/IP settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment (price/leakage) and covenant claims each with their own cap, period and threshold regime; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; delete the override language and add an express "limitations in cl 12 apply only to general Warranty Claims" provision.** The Seller's drafting would silently drag every separate regime into the 20%/18-month box.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. DL §10 admits this is only the source relied on and that Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extracts, constitution, prior transfers/issue resolutions, encumbrance (PPSR) searches, board/shareholder authority for the sale, and Riverlark security release (links to N-009). Title warranty under fundamental regime (N-004).
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone; run independent searches and require supporting documents as Completion deliverables.** DD-012 is a Company-generated internal register, not independent proof of ownership or absence of encumbrances.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN. Target a separate tax indemnity/warranty regime (longer period, higher cap) and separate IP warranties/indemnity (incl. Ironquay). Do not assume unlimited liability and do not assume resolution.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items for the next turn.** The Seller cannot settle terms unilaterally, and folding Tax/IP into a 20%/18-month general regime is inconsistent with N-004/N-014.

---

## Summary table

| ID | Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject – 25% / 6.0m (no Frost authority for fallback) |
| 002 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | Reject – 5k / 50k / first dollar |
| 003 | Time limit | 18 months + override rider | Reject – 24 months; delete rider |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Reject – 100% / 6 yrs / outside basket |
| 005 | Fraud | No carve-out; "all Claims" | Reject – full carve-out (non-negotiable) |
| 006 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Reject – specific fair disclosure only |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable", advisers | Reject – delete |
| 008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent on delivery | Reject – hard CP with evidence of conditions |
| 009 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject – payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Not itemised | Reject – specific seller-funded line + on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Reject – broaden; cure/assignment pre-Completion |
| 012 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject characterisation – investigation covenants + specific indemnity |
| 013 | Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Hold – assess; no pre-judged treatment |
| 014 | Category separation | General regime overrides all | Reject – express separation |
| 015 | Title | DD-012 register | Reject – independent evidence |
| 016 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – remain open |

## Items requiring principal decision (Amelia Frost)
None of the Seller's positions is currently acceptable without principal sign-off. Specifically flag: (i) whether any fallback on cap (20%) or claims period (18 months) is to be authorised in writing for this draft – **currently none is**; and (ii) whether any post-Completion Riverlark release structure would ever be entertained (would require irrevocable undertaking + her approval).

## Next steps
1. Send mark-up rejecting cl 8.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5 override language, Sched 7 general disclosure, and inserting fraud carve-out and category-separation clause.
2. Request: Bluefen consent + cl 11.3 evidence; Riverlark payout letter and discharge form; Ironquay payment evidence/assignment; DD-006 investigation log and status; DD-008/DD-011 renewal documents; full title pack.
3. Commission independent ASIC/PPSR searches on Paperbark Analytics.
4. Revise funds flow to include DD-005 bonuses and on-costs and Riverlark repayment.
=== END ADVICE ===
